call_points.text: FY28 revenue goal of ₹6,000 Cr could be reached earlier than 2028 if the current momentum holds.
High-teens revenue growth in FY27 looks feasible on the current run rate, subject to US demand.
Business can inherently generate 10-12% EBITDA; management targets that band by FY28.
Gross margin rose to 51.5% from 46% on outerwear mix and value-added overseas output; called sustainable on the same mix.
Bangladesh adds 6-7 million pieces by September, taking group installed capacity to about 108 million pieces.
FY27 capex outlined at ₹200-250 Cr across geographies; detailed plan to follow.
Container shortages and freight spot prices are rising before peak season; customers pay freight on FOB terms.
Board approved a 1:1 bonus issue, subject to shareholder approval.
Management maintains the FY28 target of reaching 125-130 million pieces capacity and ₹6,000+ Cr revenue.
FY27 EBITDA margin is guided at 10% to 12% range, supported by cost restructuring and easing tariff pressures.
Committed capex for FY27 is outlined at ₹200 Cr to ₹250 Cr across geographies, following ₹250 Cr in FY26.

penalties.authority: Collector of Stamp, Government of NCT of Delhi
penalties.details: Proceedings were initiated by the Collector of Stamps, Government of NCT of Delhi, under the provisions of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as applicable to the National Capital Territory of Delhi, for determination of the stamp duty payable in connection with the issuance/allotment of equity shares . Pursuant to the said proceedings, order dated August 25, 2026 was passed by the competent authority under Sections 33, 38 and 40 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, adjudging the Company liable to pay stamp duty of Rs. 6,088/- (Rupees Six Thousand Eighty Eight only), along with a penalty of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only). The Company has paid the aforesaid stamp duty and penalty.
penalties.impact: There has been no significant impact on financial, operational or other activities of the Company.

operating_notes.text: Installed capacity reached 101 million pieces per annum in FY26.
Average realisation per piece was ₹735 in Q1FY27 versus ₹715 in Q1FY26 and ₹643 for full-year FY26.
Bangladesh is about 45%+ of group volume, with Vietnam and India each around 22-27%.
India utilisation was 65-70% in Q1FY27 with efficiency of 50-58%; overseas locations ran at 75-80% of quarterly available capacity.
Vin Pearl Global Vietnam Limited incorporated Great Pearl Vietnam Global Limited in Vietnam with an initial investment of USD 1.2 million.

timeline.summary: Pearl Global Industries promoters submitted the annual Regulation 31(4) shareholding declaration for FY26 on April 3, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,313.58 Cr (+6.9% YoY), net profit ₹80.98 Cr (+24.6% YoY).
Shilpa Saraf (ICSI M. No.: ACS-23564) uploaded the audio recording of the Q4FY26 earnings conference call on May 15, 2026.
Pearl Global reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹5,025 Cr and PAT of ₹270 Cr, achieving 101 million pieces capacity.
On 6 August 2026 Pearl Global's Q1FY27 call reported revenue of ₹1,528 Cr (up 24.5% YoY), EBITDA margin of 10.7% and PAT of ₹99 Cr, with a 1:1 bonus issue approved subject to shareholder approval.
Pearl Global Industries announced that its step-down subsidiary incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary in Vietnam, Great Pearl Vietnam Global Limited, with an initial investment of USD 1.2 million.

watchlist.response: Haryana wage revision hit the quarter; without it margin would be 9%+, and the target is high single-digit to double-digit EBITDA in India.
watchlist.text: Standalone EBITDA margin fell 70 bps YoY despite record gross margins; will India reach 8.5-9%?

watchlist.response: Higher job work and outsourcing manufacturing expenses in line with volume; gross margin improvement from product mix is sustainable.
watchlist.text: Other expenses up 51% YoY alongside gross margin jump from 46% to 51.5%

watchlist.response: Net working capital days unchanged at 43-44; more internal cash used for working capital, finance cost targeted at 1.7-1.8% of sales.
watchlist.text: Finance cost growth has tapered; does that mean receivable days will rise?

watchlist.response: On the contrary, retailers remain conservative and order closer to sale; no trend of early ordering.
watchlist.text: Will customers shift to longer-term ordering cycles given disruptions?
